title: Public systems can deliver large-scale gains, but uneven progress and compounding crises are pushing many development outcomes off track
source_unit: UN DESA, The Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026
geography: Global and regional monitoring of the 2030 Agenda using the UN global indicator framework

observations.period: 2015-2025; public-system gains across selected global SDG indicators

denominator.unit: global SDG monitoring frame with selected indicators and regional aggregates

safely_managed_water_gain.unit: approximately additional people gaining access to safely managed drinking water since 2015

safely_managed_sanitation_gain.unit: approximately additional people gaining access to safely managed sanitation since 2015

electricity_access.unit: percent of the world's population with electricity access

internet_access_change.unit: global population internet-access share change since 2015

social_protection_coverage.unit: share of global population covered by at least one social-protection benefit, reported as a first historical majority

observations.method: UN DESA compilation of the latest available official and international-agency data under the global SDG indicator framework, with selected global and regional aggregates.
observations.uncertainty: Indicator definitions, time coverage, data availability, and national reporting quality differ across goals; aggregate access does not establish reliability, affordability, adequacy, quality, or equal use.
observations.subgroup: Populations gaining or lacking water, sanitation, electricity, internet, and social-protection access across countries, regions, income groups, and other unequal exposure categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage gains can coexist with intermittent service, exclusion, unaffordable use, unsafe quality, weak remedy, or unequal distribution; access is not the same as usable outcome.

denominator.unit: SDG targets with sufficient trend data for the report's global progress assessment

on_track_or_moderate.unit: percent of targets on track or showing moderate progress

too_slow.unit: percent of targets advancing too slowly

regressed.unit: percent of targets regressed below 2015 baselines

observations.method: UN DESA assessment of available trend data for 139 SDG targets, compared with 2015 baselines and target trajectories.
observations.uncertainty: Only targets with sufficient trend data enter this assessment; percentages summarize target trajectories and should not be read as a single population-weighted welfare score.
observations.subgroup: Countries, regions, institutions, and populations affected by different SDG trajectories, data availability, conflict, climate, debt, financing, and implementation capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: The aggregate trajectory does not mean every goal is stalled: progress can be rapid in some sectors and places while regression or stagnation persists elsewhere.

observations.period: 2025-2026; development pressure, exclusion, and implementation capacity

denominator.unit: global SDG challenge and implementation-capacity frame

out_of_school.unit: children and young people remaining out of school globally

youth_neet.unit: approximately percent of young people aged 15-24 not in employment, education, or training

oda_decline.unit: percent change in official development assistance in 2025, reported as a record annual decline

urban_informal_settlement.unit: approximately people living in slums or informal settlements

forcibly_displaced.unit: people forcibly displaced as of December 2025

observations.method: UN DESA synthesis of education, youth transition, development finance, housing, displacement, conflict, climate, and institutional implementation indicators.
observations.uncertainty: These indicators use different reference dates and definitions and cannot be summed into one composite burden; causation and local implementation pathways require separate evidence.
observations.subgroup: Children and youth, informal-settlement residents, displaced populations, aid-dependent countries, conflict-affected communities, and governments with constrained fiscal or institutional capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate pressure can be reduced through targeted investment, peace, data systems, technology access, international cooperation, and scaling proven interventions; the report is not a claim of inevitable failure.

related_sources.claim: Indicator framework, data vintage, and interpretation notes.

boundary: This record adds a public-system-results-to-uneven-progress, implementation-capacity, and crisis-pressure route. It is not a respondent-level dataset, does not measure service reliability or individual benefit receipt, and does not establish that any single crisis caused a specific SDG trajectory.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN DESA publication page, UN SDG report platform, press release, report PDF URL, and note-to-reader were retrieved; global gains, target trajectory shares, out-of-school, youth transition, aid, informal-settlement, and displacement claims were cross-checked against official materials.
